comments.value:
Currently, groups can host Group or Group+ instances with custom worlds with rules/consent banners at world spawn with a button that needs to be pressed to continue. Some groups decide to restrict Group instance access to specific roles at instance creation time, which is enforced by the system.

Groups may uphold their group rules by hosting Group-only instances, which requires membership in the group. This typically requires the user to read and agree to the group's Rules section represented by VRChat client and website before getting membership in the group and to be able to join Group-only instances; however, some people use third-party tools such as VRCX to accept group membership invites and therefore may not get to see the group Rules.

@{68098a4626271974ef4d2775|full_name}  Yes that information is correct, however I would like to note some additional caveats:

Not all worlds support these types of custom banners, and even if the rules are made as a Sticker, there is no way to verify if the user has read the rules or can even see the rules board. It also complicates the reporting process when VRChat is unable to know whether or not a user was exposed to the rules ar any point in time after joining the instance, or if they are submitting false reports.

The other issue is regarding Group+ and Group-only instances, as those follow Private instance rules and as such may have a more refined or specific set of rules, conduct, and guidelines which may differ from what users may be expecting from most instances. These are not able to be made discoverable in any way which would allow users to find the groups hosting these instances and check them out to join them. Group Publics do not seem to follow in terms of Private Instance guidelines, even if age restricted or with up-front rules, which means they may sometimes only serve to drive up interest as opposed to functioning as a standard group meeting or event.

Group rules, descriptions, and “tags” can also not be searched, so you cannot very easily find groups which allow or prohibit certain things and join them. Even if you do find them, there is no way to know if they actively host any instances apart from checking Posts or any related social media links after already having joined the group.

details:
Group instance discovery is a complicated issue, particularly when you would like to hold group events with specific rules, and do not want to allow users who are not a part of the group (nor have not read the rules) to join. It is also not easy to advertise your group in a way that can be seen in the client.

This post proposes an optional "Discoverable" option for all group instance types. There should be a new Tab in the Group menu where you can discover instances that are hosted by groups. If the instance is Group or Group+, the user is required to first read the rules, and request to join. Once their request has been accepted, the notification will give them an option to view and join the instances.

Not only does this greatly enhance discoverability for many groups, but it enables stronger enforcement of group rules, and also allows users to find **active** groups which regularly host instances. This toggle should be optional.
title: Group Instance Discoverability
